title: Capture a view as a PNG image and publish the file
task: Render a Revit view to a PNG image file so it can be seen or screenshotted: set the view's DisplayStyle, build ImageExportOptions with the view in SetViewsAndSheets and BOTH file-type fields set, call Document.ExportImage, find the file Revit actually wrote (it appends the view name to FilePath), and Connector.Publish it so the image comes back to the caller.

pitfalls.symptom: Exporting a shaded 3D view (ShadingWithEdges/Realistic) writes NO file and throws NO exception; Connector.Publish then finds nothing.
pitfalls.cause: A shaded view's image is governed by ImageExportOptions.ShadowViewsFileType, while a wireframe/HLR view uses HLRandWFViewsFileType; if only one is set, the other display style silently produces no file.
pitfalls.fix: Set BOTH HLRandWFViewsFileType AND ShadowViewsFileType (e.g. ImageFileType.PNG) so any display style produces a file.

pitfalls.symptom: The file at ImageExportOptions.FilePath does not exist after ExportImage.
pitfalls.cause: Revit treats FilePath as a STEM and appends ' - <ViewType> - <ViewName>.<ext>', so the real filename differs from what you set.
pitfalls.fix: After ExportImage, glob the export directory for '<stem>*' to find the file Revit actually wrote, then Publish that path.

pitfalls.symptom: Calling ExportImage inside a Connector.WithTransaction block fails with script-target-must-not-be-modifiable.
pitfalls.cause: ExportImage (like Document.Export) is self-transacting and requires the target document not to be modifiable.
pitfalls.fix: Set the view's DisplayStyle inside a block, then call ExportImage at top level BETWEEN blocks.
